{"findings":[{"kind":"defect","severity":"medium","title":"Guard drops coverage attribute on netstandard2.0 and .NET Framework","detail":"Every template wraps the attribute in #if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK. The comment in the test and the README say this is because the attribute is missing on those targets, but that is not true. System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute exists in .NET Framework 4.0 and later and in netstandard2.0, and classes are a valid target there. Only the Assembly target was added later, and the generator never uses it. So consumers that build for netstandard2.0 or .NET Framework never get the attribute, and their generated formatters and resolvers still show up in coverage reports. That breaks F1 ('All generated code is decorated') and F2 for a large group of users: libraries targeting netstandard2.0, Unity projects and net4x apps. The guard buys nothing for N1, because the attribute would compile on those targets without it. The README states the same wrong reason in h1. The new test ExcludeAttributeIsGuardedForTargetsWhereItIsUnavailable makes the guard a required pattern, so it would fail if the guard were removed.
